measuredOn.metric: corpus-f published metric (lib.ts normalizedSignalErrors, MATCH_THRESHOLD 0.01), unchanged
measuredOn.tool: pnpm exec tsx benchmarks/corpus/corpus-f/triage-detail.ts <fixture-id> [--tmax s] [--deck variant] [--reference-tmax s [--candidate ngspice]]
measuredOn.diagnosticLimitations: Fine-step runs do not establish step convergence. Reference-TMAX comparisons use each candidate's own grid and breakpoint alignment, so their maxima do not rank engine accuracy on a common grid.

rootCauses.summary: MOS1 treats CBD/CBS as constant capacitors and silently ignores CJ/CJSW/MJ/MJSW/PB/FC; ngspice-47 uses voltage-dependent depletion capacitance.
MOS1 has no Meyer intrinsic gate capacitance from TOX; only constant CGSO/CGDO overlaps are stamped.
The transient metric interpolates ngspice's coarse default-step output onto spice-ts points, so ngspice's own truncation and interpolation error is scored as a spice-ts mismatch.
Signals with zero or ~100 uV ngspice peaks are normalised by that peak (floor 1e-12), so fV-uV residuals exceed 1%.
BSIM1/BSIM2 (LEVEL 4/5) are not implemented. Since #552 they raise UnsupportedModelLevelError instead of silently running Level-1 equations, which caused the issue-table mismatch.
The .model VDMOS card was silently dropped. #542 made unsupported model types a typed error and #562 (#506) added the ngspice-47 VDMOS model; both VDMOS decks now match.
